name: Sterling-Nakamura Diplomatic Immunity Bracelet DIB-1
description: A wrist-worn device that continuously broadcasts a verified diplomatic immunity credentials signal recognized by law enforcement systems throughout GLMZ. The DIB-1 contains a quantum-encrypted identity chip that authenticates the wearer's diplomatic status to any scanner or automated system, triggering legal protections that prevent detention, search, or arrest. The bracelet's signal is recognized by autonomous security systems, which stand down when detecting a valid diplomatic credential. Sterling-Nakamura issues them to senior personnel and allied diplomatic staff — the bracelet does not make the wearer invincible, but it makes detaining them a significant legal and political event.

specifications.recognition: Compatible with all GLMZ law enforcement systems

story_hooks: A DIB-1 was used by a murder suspect to walk through a crime scene perimeter — the automated security systems stood down and human officers hesitated to challenge a diplomatic credential, giving the suspect time to escape.

A counterfeit DIB-1 has appeared that broadcasts a valid-seeming diplomatic credential — the forgery is good enough to fool automated systems but will not survive manual verification, creating a narrow window of false immunity.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist wrist band with an almost jewelry-like appearance, betraying its critical function through subtle technological detailing. The bracelet sits flush against the skin with an air of understated corporate authority. Its polished surface catches light in a way that makes it appear both expensive and intimidating.
physical_description.weight_description: Featherweight (50g) — barely noticeable when worn, feels like high-end smart jewelry rather than security hardware
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium alloy with inlaid quantum-encrypted biometric module
physical_description.finish: Mirror-polished satin with ceramic-coated accent stripe; anti-reflective matte panel on ventral side housing the biometric sensor
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with Sterling-Nakamura's signature platinum accent stripe running axially along the band; faint bioluminescent teal glow emanating from the biometric window during active broadcast
physical_description.interface_elements: Minimal — a small translucent sapphire window (5mm diameter) on the inner wrist showing status indicator (solid teal = broadcasting, amber = low battery, red = tamper alert); micro-haptic feedback pulses along the band for alerts; no visible buttons or ports (induction charging via contact points)
distinctive_features: Faint quantum encryption indicator — a slowly pulsing geometric Φ symbol visible through the sapphire window
Seamless titanium construction with no visible seams or fasteners
Subtle 'STERLING-NAKAMURA' etched along the inner surface in micro-text, only visible under magnification
A hair-thin wire embedded along the band's circumference — the broadcast antenna, invisible unless light hits at the right angle
Micro-perforations around the biometric window for environmental monitoring
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Corporate holographic security seal embossed on inner band (only readable with IR scanner); tiny regulatory GLMZ compliance stamp barely visible on the rear edge
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine and meticulously maintained — diplomatic staff keep these polished like mirrors. Occasional micro-scratches on the brushed surface from daily wear, but the teal biometric glow always remains active and steady, a constant reminder of the wearer's legal standing.
